vBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2095: pan reload builds stale primary worktree source (divergent from origin/main) — landed strike fixes never go live

plan.title: bug(deploy): pan reload builds stale primary worktree source (divergent from origin/main) — landed strike fixes never go live
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-4-8

narratives.Problem: `pan reload` runs `bun install` + `npm run build` inside `process.cwd()` (the primary worktree) with NO git sync — see reload.ts runCommand (reload.ts:36-45, no cwd override), runBuild (reload.ts:59-61), and reloadCommand's production build block (reload.ts:146-164). The primary worktree's local main is routinely diverged from origin/main: many `chore(beads/state/records)` auto-commits AHEAD, and 1-2 landed CI-green strike fixes BEHIND. So a freshly landed fix on origin/main is NOT in the build source, and `pan reload` compiles + deploys the STALE code while reporting success ('landed != live'). Evidence (RUN-20): strike 0973c8c8d (PAN-2094, ohmypi 30s->120s timeout) landed on origin/main; `pan reload` reported healthy but the deployed dist still had 30s, and ohmypi spawns kept orphaning at 30s. `git rev-list --left-right --count origin/main...HEAD` = origin 1-2, HEAD 61. This is the PAN-1723 family: post-merge-deploy.sh was fixed to build from a pristine origin/main worktree, but the interactive/flywheel `pan reload` path never got the same treatment.
narratives.Proposal: Make `pan reload`'s production build path build from origin/main, mirroring the proven scripts/post-merge-deploy.sh pattern (PAN-1723). Before building: resolve the true primary repo root, then `git fetch origin main`. Gate on `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main HEAD`: if origin/main IS an ancestor of HEAD (HEAD already contains every origin/main commit) build in place as today; else (origin/main has commits not in HEAD -> behind/diverged) create a throwaway detached worktree checked out at origin/main, run `bun install` + `npm run build` there, and swap the built dist/ into the primary repo root (near-atomic same-filesystem rename) before restarting. Any failure (fetch, worktree add, install, build) leaves the old server running. The throwaway worktree is always removed in finally{}. The `pan dev` SIGUSR2 hot-reload path and `pan reload --skip-build` are untouched. scripts/post-merge-deploy.sh is already correct and is NOT modified.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Do NOT modify the `pan dev` SIGUSR2 hot-reload path (reload.ts:106-131) — local divergence is expected in dev mode.
- Do NOT modify scripts/post-merge-deploy.sh — it already builds from a pristine origin/main worktree (PAN-1723).
- Do NOT change `pan reload --skip-build` behavior — it bypasses the build entirely.
- Do NOT add a --local / --force-local-build opt-out flag (deliberately out of scope per the PRD).
- Do NOT push, pull, merge, or otherwise mutate the primary main branch's HEAD or working tree — the fix reads origin/main into a throwaway worktree and never touches the operator's primary checkout.
- Do NOT address auto-commit churn that causes local main to run ahead of origin — that is PAN-2375's domain (belt-and-suspenders).

autoDecisions.summary: Base the plan on the existing authoritative PRD draft .pan/drafts/PAN-2095.md rather than re-deriving an approach.
autoDecisions.rationale: The PRD (2026-07-04) is a verified implementation brief that matches the code (reload.ts + post-merge-deploy.sh) exactly and follows the Overdeck 'PRD is the implementation brief' convention.

autoDecisions.summary: Use `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main HEAD` for the divergence gate instead of exact SHA equality.
autoDecisions.rationale: FR-3 requires the worktree path only when origin/main has commits NOT in HEAD. The ancestor check matches that intent exactly and builds in place whenever HEAD already contains origin/main (the common ahead-only state-sync case), avoiding needless worktree builds that the PRD's sample exact-equality check would trigger.

autoDecisions.summary: Do NOT add a --local / --force-local-build opt-out flag.
autoDecisions.rationale: The PRD explicitly scopes it out. The in-place build path is preserved for the aligned case; unpushed local src commits on primary main violate push-discipline and are covered by PAN-2375, so the pristine origin/main build is the intended 'landed -> live' default.

autoDecisions.summary: Resolve the primary repo root (git rev-parse --show-toplevel + workspace->primary regex) before building.
autoDecisions.rationale: Mirrors post-merge-deploy.sh:42-45 so `pan reload` targets the singleton host dashboard's dist even when invoked from a workspace or a subdirectory.

items.title: Build `pan reload` from origin/main when the primary HEAD is behind/diverged

expected_outputs: reload.test.ts passes including the new aligned/diverged/failure/cleanup cases

narrative.Action: In src/cli/commands/reload.ts, replace the inline production build (the `if (!options.skipBuild)` block at reload.ts:134-164 that calls runBunInstall() then runBuild() in process.cwd()) with a new async helper `buildFromOriginMain(repoRoot)`. Steps: (1) add async git support via `promisify(exec)` — a `runGitAsync(args, cwd)` helper (NFR-1: no execSync); (2) `git fetch origin main` in repoRoot (a fetch failure is a warning, then fall back to in-place build); (3) gate with `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main HEAD`: exit 0 (ancestor) -> `bun install` + `npm run build` in place (unchanged behavior, preserves H1); exit 1 -> print the divergence warning with the origin/main short sha (FR-4), create `join(dirname(repoRoot), '.pan-reload-build-'+process.pid)` as a detached worktree at origin/main (H2/H6), run `bun install` + `npm run build` with cwd set to that worktree (H1), then swap its dist/ into repoRoot via same-filesystem rename (mv dist -> dist.old.pid, cp -a worktree/dist -> dist, rm dist.old) and print the built sha (FR-4); (4) remove the worktree in finally{} on success AND failure (FR-5/H4). Any git/install/build failure throws; reloadCommand catches, records failure via recordReloadStatus, sets process.exitCode=1, and RETURNS before restartDashboard so the old server keeps running (H3). Keep the existing dashboardBundleMtimeMs() before/after guard. Do NOT touch the SIGUSR2 dev path (reload.ts:106-131) or the --skip-build early-out (FR-6/FR-7). Keep reload.ts under ~300 lines; extract the helper to a sibling module if needed (D4). Add tests to reload.test.ts (extend its existing spawn/exec mocks) covering the diverged, aligned, failure-preserves-server, and worktree-cleanup paths.

items.title: Given origin/main has commits not in the primary HEAD (behind/diverged), when `pan reload` runs without --skip-build, it creates a detached git worktree checked out at origin/main, runs the build in that worktree, and swaps that worktree's dist/ into the repo root before restarting the dashboard
Given origin/main is already an ancestor of the primary HEAD, when `pan reload` runs, it builds in place (runs `bun install` + `npm run build` in the repo root) and creates no throwaway worktree

When `git fetch origin main`, the worktree `bun install`, or `npm run build` fails, `pan reload` exits with a non-zero code, records a failed reload status, and does NOT restart the dashboard (the running server is preserved)
The throwaway build worktree is removed (`git worktree remove --force`) after reload whether the build succeeds or throws, leaving no leaked entry in `git worktree list`
When it builds from origin/main, `pan reload` prints the origin/main short sha it built so the deployed sha is observable in the reload output
Resolve the primary repo root before building so `pan reload` from a workspace/subdir targets the host dashboard

expected_outputs: reload.test.ts passes including the repo-root resolution case

narrative.Action: Before calling buildFromOriginMain, compute the primary repo root instead of using process.cwd() raw. Resolve `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from process.cwd(); then apply the workspace->primary rule mirroring scripts/post-merge-deploy.sh:42-45 — if the toplevel matches `(.+)/workspaces/feature-[^/]+$`, use the captured parent as the repo root. Pass the resolved root into buildFromOriginMain so the fetch, worktree, build, and dist swap all target the singleton host dashboard's checkout even when `pan reload` is invoked from a workspace or a subdirectory. When invoked from the primary root, the resolved root is unchanged. Add a unit test asserting a workspace-style cwd resolves to the parent primary root. This bead depends on reload-build-from-origin-main (it refines that helper's repoRoot input).

items.title: Given `pan reload` is invoked from a workspace path matching …/workspaces/feature-pan-XXX or a subdirectory, it resolves the primary repo root (via git rev-parse --show-toplevel plus the workspace->primary regex) and fetches/builds/swaps that primary repo's dist, not the workspace's
A unit test asserts that a workspace-style cwd (…/workspaces/feature-pan-123) resolves to its parent primary repo root and that root is the one passed into the build helper
When invoked from the primary repo root, reload uses that root unchanged (no workspace rewrite applied)
